images.alt: A blue-violet SGI Indy workstation photographed from the front against a white background
images.caption: The Indy's blue-violet "pizza box" case, introduced by SGI in July 1993 as its entry-level workstation.

images.alt: A complete SGI Indy workstation with its original 17-inch CRT monitor, keyboard and mouse
images.caption: A full Indy system as SGI shipped it: pizza-box unit, CRT, keyboard and mouse, priced for universities and design studios to buy by the dozen.

images.alt: An SGI Indy workstation with its original IndyCam video camera attached on top
images.caption: The camera on top is the IndyCam — SGI put digital video capture in the box rather than on the options list, unusual for 1993.

images.alt: A close-up of an SGI IndyCam, the small video camera bundled with the Indy workstation
images.caption: The IndyCam, 1993 — a standard-issue peripheral that made the Indy one of the first desktop machines built for video from day one.

images.alt: The rear panel of an SGI Indy workstation showing its ports and connectors
images.caption: The Indy's back panel carried the ports for the era's new desktop expectation: networked, graphical, and increasingly video-capable.
